P1.evidence: No setter suffix in the title and no setter referenced on the call, so the read-back is not applicable. Frame was three-part, not four: 'I just want to understand, like, what's going on, what have you tried, and where are trying to get to' — no 'what's in the way' or 'what you need'. Agreement was taken ('yeah?' / 'Yeah.') and the call opened with 'what's the main thing you're trying to fix right now?'

P2.evidence: Age (35), height (6'3") and weight (220 lb) were all volunteered in passing and never asked for. Health conditions, hereditary or own, were never asked at all — only injuries were ('do you have like any injuries or like anything that limits your movement?'). Sleep and daily energy were never touched; the rep asked what time he wakes but not how he sleeps. Work, training week, results and diet were covered well and with follow-up.

P3.evidence: Good surface work — 'What's the goal that you're looking to achieve right now?' and 'Results in what way? You mean an appearance?' The deep bridge was run well: 'what's the biggest reason you want to actually draw the line in the sand and get this body right now?' produced the baby. But the meaning question stalled — 'what would that moment mean to you' got 'I haven't even really thought about that too much' and the rep let it go instead of pressing. 'Who else does that impact?' was never asked; the family angle was volunteered. Reflect-back landed: the rep summarised the future-proofing frame and got 'Yeah, exactly.'

P4.evidence: Strongest phase of the call. 'have you tried anything else in the past? Like any other coaching programs?', 'how did that work out for you?', and a persistent 'but let me understand why' that would not accept 'I blame it on the puppy'. The gap question was posed as a binary (home-training barrier vs accountability) rather than open, but the prospect named it himself: 'I honestly think it was just more of like a, yeah, like an accountability issue.' The 'the information isn't the problem' line was never used.

P5.evidence: The two-year cost-of-inaction question was never asked; instead the rep asked for an aspirational six-month picture. 'Draw the line in the sand' was used verbatim but as a motivation question, not as a commitment close. The only settle-for challenge came after the price and was a one-liner — 'Come on, Kurt, don't do that. Keep yourself to the highest standard.' — with no 'why not?' follow-up. The prospect's own summary going into the price was 'my status quo currently isn't terrible', which is exactly what this phase exists to dismantle.

P6.evidence: P6a run cleanly: 'If you had the right training, simple nutrition dialed in, and real accountability from Trevor and all built around your life, would you agree that you would get to your goals?' Isolation was run twice, once as a 1-10 scale ('apart from the numbers, you're a 10 at this' — 'Yeah, I would say so'). But the yes was soft — 'I think so, yeah' then 'Well, yes' — and the rep noticed it ('the first time it didn't sound so sure') and still moved to price rather than returning to Phase 5.

P11.evidence: No agreement was reached, so payment, the Trevor onboarding booking, the agreement email and the welcome/Skool steps were never reachable.

objection_plays.detail: Isolation ran — 'Apart from the finances that we're discussing right now, is there anything else that would be stopping you from getting in?' — and the payment-plan door was opened almost verbatim ('most of the clients take care of the investment upfront, for certain clients ... we can break it up'). Everything after that was skipped: no 'you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place', no permission question for an honest financial conversation, and none of the six financial-picture questions. The one probe at cash on hand ('is it that you don't have this cash on you right now') got 'Not necessarily' and was abandoned rather than followed. Instead the rep jumped to a $1,200 trial and then to credit-card points.

The prospect gave a clean not-the-right-time trigger — 'post-summer, when everything is accounted for ... at least it's a no for right now' — anchored to a house addition finishing in the fall. None of the OD moves ran: no 'things never slow down', no 'the longer you wait the harder this gets', no 'the only thing you can control is right now'. The rep accepted the timeline and pivoted to the downsell.

Reduced-scope objection with no scripted play. The prospect asked three separate times for a stripped-down product — prescribed workouts without meal planning or 24-7 access — and the script has no tier or response for it. The rep improvised a $1,200 30-day trial, which the prospect read as still being the wrong shape, and only mentioned Primal University at $200/month after the loss was already conceded. This is a script gap, not a rep failure: the ladder exists but there is no scripted moment to introduce it.

Cheaper alternative that is working. The prospect's $160/month gym plus a self-programmed backyard setup is genuinely delivering — he is training three times a week and recently PR'd. The script assumes the blocker is capacity to pay rather than perceived value against a functioning substitute, so the rep had nothing to run and fell back on 'you're not buying a gym membership, you're buying a transformation'.

notes: The discovery and root-cause work was genuinely good and the prospect named his own accountability gap unprompted — then the rep went to price without ever building a cost of inaction, so the prospect walked in still believing his status quo was fine. Fix one thing: run Phase 5 properly before the number, and do not proceed on a 'I think so' at Phase 6.
